title: Cutting a recording and exporting it copies the pieces instead of re-encoding
goal: When the only edits to a recording are cuts and trims (pieces taken out or kept), exporting or saving it to MP4 should take a second or two, not a quarter of its running time, because the kept pieces can be copied across as they are instead of every frame being drawn and encoded again. Anything drawn on top (zooms, titles, captions, transitions, speed changes) still goes through the full render.
notes:
User asked: "is exporting to mp4 really that slow? ... i want to be able to record a video, make some edits and save and use it in teams really fast."

From code reading (not run): the only fast path is a byte-for-byte copy of an untouched whole recording at High, unshrunk (EditorState+VideoExport.swift:338-346); any edit re-encodes every frame through DocumentFrames + DocumentMovieWriter (:348-366). Measured today: 5 min recording at 1080p in 72-83 s (queue/audits/2026-09-27-fast-video-export.json). Approach: AVMutableComposition of the kept time ranges with AVAssetExportPresetPassthrough (or AVAssetWriter passthrough of compressed samples) for the cut-only case; non-keyframe cut points need smart rendering (re-encode the GOP head) or accept snapping and say so. Trap: the recording's colour tags (MovieColour, 2026-10-04) must survive passthrough. Trap: held frames and speed changes are NOT cut-only. Companion: 'Saving an edited recording puts the finished video in history, ready to paste' (filed same day) uses this path for its background MP4.
acceptance: Measure first: export a 3 min recording with three pieces cut out, today, and record the time in the audit

With cut/trim-only edits, MP4 export (and the save-to-history MP4 and Copy Video) copies the kept stretches without re-encoding, MEASURED under 3 s for a 3 min recording on this Mac, written in the audit

Cuts land on the exact frames the timeline shows: if a cut is not on a keyframe, only the frames from the cut to the next keyframe are re-encoded (smart render) or the audit shows why whole-segment re-encode is needed; the exported file's length and first/last frame of each piece match the timeline within one frame, MEASURED
Sound stays in sync across every cut (MEASURED drift under one frame at the end) and has no click at the joins
As soon as anything else is on the timeline (zoom, title, caption burned in, transition, speed, crop, click effects) the export uses today's full path, unchanged
The Export sheet's size estimate stays right for the fast path
Unit tests for deciding when the fast path applies; a walk exports a cut-only recording and checks duration and the time it took
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Also applies to Command S into history (saving-an-edited-recording-puts-the-finished-vid): CaptureStore.writeEditedVideo calls EditorState.writeVideo(of:pictures:...) at HistoryVideoSave.choice; a cut-only fast path in that static writer speeds both. Measured full re-encode, Retina 2880x1800 High full size: 30 s edit 15.5 s, 3 min edit ~75 s.

Adversarial pass: the mock has no export surface; a Premiere user expects Export to be instant when nothing is rendered (smart rendering), which this now is. Traps found by measurement: the recording's edit list puts its frames 70 ms late in the file (cuts are moved onto the timeline's clock); the loop's Long Talk .mov counts decode times ahead of show times (planner slides the decode clock back); Apple's encoder makes 29-frame closed groups with B-frames.

left rough: a copied file keeps the recording's 709 colour tags while a drawn one says sRGB; same as the untouched whole-file copy has always done, not seen on screen, so no task. Standard/Small/1080p/720p still draw every frame by design (they ask for a smaller file).

Cut/trim-only edits now export, Copy Video and save into history by copying the kept stretches (PhotonzCore/CutCopy.swift, PhotonzMedia/PieceCopyWriter.swift, wired in EditorState.writeVideo, commit 7c564f4f). Measured on a 3 min 2880x1800 edit with three pieces cut: 0.78 s copied vs 73.5 s drawn; Copy Video 0.84 s; history save 1.16 s; sheet size exact. Frames within one of the drawn file and exact at cuts; sound identical at every join and the end. 26+ unit tests, 4 media tests, full suite green (11,646), walk a-cut-recording-copies-its-pieces-walk plus 10 neighbouring walks green. Audit queue/audits/2026-10-07-cut-only-fast-export.json.
